evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep said 'it takes about ten minutes' but never framed the 'dependable quote' promise or waited for a yes — moved straight to name collection.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked: 'What are your biggest concerns for this upcoming move and what are the most important things you want answers to on this call today. Aside from the pricing.' Customer raised: fourth-floor apartment with elevator. Rep acknowledged with 'definitely... we move from whatever floors to another' but never asked 'tell me more about that' or dug deeper into the concern.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer: 'my biggest concern is probably, we live on the fourth floor of an apartment complex so there is an elevator.' Rep: 'Well, yeah, definitely... we can definitely take care of your remove.' One acknowledgment, no follow-up probing.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No summary reflection. Customer stated concern; rep acknowledged without reflecting back what was heard.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (apartment → townhome), floors/stories (4th floor to 2-story), rooms (1 bedroom), walking distance (both directions), additional spaces (none), special considerations (grill), full furniture inventory — all covered.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Never asked 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?'
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Asked: 'a typical one bedroom apartment? Usually has $15 to 25 [boxes] so do you feel like you will fall within that range?' Framed as typical range, not as overflow/special-items check.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Gave range: '4 and a half to 5 and a half hours with two movers and one truck. So for the pricing it's safe to budget around $1,110 to $1,340.' Personalized to fourth-floor apartment with elevator access, distance walk, moving to two-story townhome.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Trip fee disclosed upfront ($75 for out-of-zone). Stated '$115 per hour per mover,' included fuel, traps, taxes, insurance, wraps, bands, tools, no hidden fees. Did not explicitly frame 2.5-hour minimum or 15-minute-increment commitment.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Never asked 'Does that feel fair?' Customer objected to price unprompted ('that sounds really expensive') and rep did not hold silence — immediately re-explained the math.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Mentioned: 'no worries damage coverage... $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for accidental damages.' Missing: explicit 'no deductible / no fine print' framing and confirmation that it's built into the rate, not an add-on (though rep did say 'included in the early rate').
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No closing question like 'Does that put those to rest?' Customer objected to price and conversation ended without addressing the Two Promises section.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Never asked 'What's still concerning you about this move?' or any genuine final-concerns check.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Never asked 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?'
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never asked 'Would you like our help with your move?' Customer said 'I think we can find someone cheaper' and rep offered to send an email but never asked for the business.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: No booking attempted. Call ended with customer saying they may call back and rep offering to send reference email.

top_strength: Thorough discovery and logistics probing — rep gathered all essential details (origin, destination, property types, floors, distance, furniture list, box count) to support an accurate estimate.
coaching_note: After the customer objected to price, the rep abandoned the sales process entirely — no attempt to address objections, no Two Promises (On-Time or Damage Coverage), no final concerns check, no ask for the business. Train to hold the line and stay in the conversation when price resistance surfaces.
